questions.prompt: A \(0.50\,\mathrm{m}\) rod moves at \(4.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) perpendicular to a \(0.30\,\mathrm{T}\) field. Find the motional emf.
A rod has motional emf \(1.2\,\mathrm{V}\) while moving at \(3.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) through a \(0.80\,\mathrm{T}\) field. Find its length.
questions.answer: \[\n\ell=\frac{\mathcal E}{Bv}=\frac{1.2}{(0.80)(3.0)}=0.50\,\mathrm{m}\n\]

questions.prompt: A \(0.25\,\mathrm{m}\) rod moves at \(6.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) in a \(0.40\,\mathrm{T}\) field. The circuit resistance is \(3.0\,\Omega\). Find the induced current.
Positive charges in a rod move with velocity \(\vec v\) to the right through a magnetic field into the page. Which end of the rod becomes positive if the rod is vertical?
questions.answer: For positive charge, \(\vec F=q\vec v\times\vec B\). Right crossed into the page points upward. Positive charge is pushed upward, so the top end becomes positive.

questions.prompt: A rod of length \(0.60\,\mathrm{m}\) moves at \(5.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), but only the velocity component perpendicular to the rod and field is \(3.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). If \(B=0.20\,\mathrm{T}\), find \(|\mathcal E|\).
questions.answer:
Use only the perpendicular speed:
\[
|\mathcal E|=B\ell v_\perp=(0.20)(0.60)(3.0)=0.36\,\mathrm{V}
\]

questions.prompt: A sliding rod has \(B=0.50\,\mathrm{T}\), \(\ell=0.40\,\mathrm{m}\), \(v=2.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and total resistance \(0.80\,\Omega\). Find the magnetic drag force.
For the rod in the previous style of setup, derive \(F=B^2\ell^2v/R\) for the magnetic drag force.
questions.answer:
The current is
\[
I= rac{B\ell v}{R}
\]
The magnetic force on the rod is
\[
F=I\ell B
\]
Substitute the current:
\[
F= rac{B\ell v}{R}\ell B= rac{B^2\ell^2v}{R}
\]

questions.prompt: Show that the mechanical power needed to pull a sliding rod at constant speed equals the electrical power dissipated.
questions.answer:
Using
\[
F= rac{B^2\ell^2v}{R}
\]
mechanical power is
\[
P_{\mathrm{mech}}=Fv= rac{B^2\ell^2v^2}{R}
\]
The induced current is
\[
I= rac{B\ell v}{R}
\]
so
\[
I^2R=\left( rac{B\ell v}{R}ight)^2R= rac{B^2\ell^2v^2}{R}
\]
Thus \(P_{\mathrm{mech}}=I^2R\).

questions.prompt: A rod moves on rails so the loop area is \(A=\ell x\). If \(x=vt\), derive the emf magnitude from Faraday's law.
questions.answer:
The flux is
\[
\Phi_B=B\ell x=B\ell vt
\]
Therefore
\[
|\mathcal E|=\left| rac{d\Phi_B}{dt}ight|=B\ell v
\]

questions.prompt: A \(0.30\,\mathrm{m}\) rod moves through a \(0.90\,\mathrm{T}\) field at unknown speed. The emf is \(0.81\,\mathrm{V}\). Find the speed.
A rod moves parallel to a magnetic field. What is the motional emf across the rod?
questions.answer: It is zero. The magnetic force is \(q\vec v\times\vec B\), and the cross product is zero when \(\vec v\) is parallel to \(\vec B\).

questions.prompt: A vertical rod moves right through a field out of the page. Which end becomes positive?
questions.answer: For positive charges, right crossed out of the page points downward. Positive charge accumulates at the bottom end, so the bottom becomes positive.

questions.prompt: A rod of length \(\ell\) rotates about one end with angular speed \(\omega\) in a uniform field perpendicular to the plane of rotation. Derive the emf between its ends.
questions.answer:
A small element at radius \(r\) has speed \(v=\omega r\), so
\[
d\mathcal E=Bv\,dr=B\omega r\,dr
\]
Integrate from \(0\) to \(\ell\):
\[
\mathcal E=\int_0^\ell B\omega r\,dr= rac{1}{2}B\omega\ell^2
\]

questions.prompt: A \(0.50\,\mathrm{m}\) rod rotates about one end at \(12\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}\) in a perpendicular \(0.20\,\mathrm{T}\) field. Find the emf between its ends.
questions.answer:
For a rotating rod,
\[
\mathcal E= rac{1}{2}B\omega\ell^2
\]
Thus
\[
\mathcal E= rac{1}{2}(0.20)(12)(0.50^2)=0.30\,\mathrm{V}
\]

questions.prompt: A sliding rod circuit has resistance \(R\). If its speed doubles, by what factors do emf, current, drag force, and dissipated power change?
questions.answer: \(\mathcal E=B\ell v\), so emf doubles. Current \(I=\mathcal E/R\) doubles. Drag force \(F=I\ell B\) doubles. Power \(P=I^2R\) increases by a factor of \(4\).

questions.prompt: A sliding rod in a field is pulled by a constant external force. Explain why it can reach a terminal speed.
questions.answer: The induced current grows with speed: \(I=B\ell v/R\). The magnetic drag force is \(F_B=B^2\ell^2v/R\), also proportional to speed. Terminal speed occurs when magnetic drag equals the applied force, so the net force becomes zero.

questions.prompt: Find the terminal speed of a sliding rod pulled by constant force \(F\) in field \(B\), length \(\ell\), and circuit resistance \(R\).
questions.answer:
At terminal speed,
\[
F= rac{B^2\ell^2v_t}{R}
\]
so
\[
v_t= rac{FR}{B^2\ell^2}
\]

questions.prompt: A rod of length \(\ell\) moves with velocity making angle \(\alpha\) to the direction perpendicular to the rod and field. Write the emf magnitude.
questions.answer:
Only the component of velocity perpendicular to the rod and field contributes: \(v_\perp=v\cos\alpha\). Therefore
\[
|\mathcal E|=B\ell v\cos\alpha
\]

questions.prompt: A conducting rod moves in a magnetic field but is not part of a closed circuit. Explain what is still physically present.
questions.answer: Magnetic force separates charges in the rod, so there is a potential difference and motional emf between its ends. There is no sustained current because there is no closed conducting path.

questions.prompt: A sliding rod of mass \(m\) starts at speed \(v_0\) with no external pull. The magnetic drag force is \(F=-(B^2\ell^2/R)v\). Derive \(v(t)\).
questions.answer:
Newton's second law gives
\[
m rac{dv}{dt}=- rac{B^2\ell^2}{R}v
\]
Separate variables:
\[
 rac{dv}{v}=- rac{B^2\ell^2}{mR}dt
\]
Integrate and use \(v(0)=v_0\):
\[
v(t)=v_0e^{-B^2\ell^2t/(mR)}
\]
